title: Artificial ethology: the fly as answer key, the observer as machine
summary: The webcam-fly line now has an explicit three-stage history. Smartfly is the earlier embodied controller: a live-video creature whose brightness/texture measurements perturb coupled rhythms and a homeostatic control index, which then drives speed and turning. Smarfly2 deliberately reverses the emphasis by keeping the organism small and moving the difficult computation into an outside observer that must infer hidden temporal state from visible evidence and behavior; its sequencing-observer branch tests selective event deposits, rhythmic continuation windows, contextual susceptibility, route closure and publication separation against simpler controls. FlyBench then treats the old fly behavior as a black box with a hidden answer key, auditing which apparent stories survive and which collapse under controlled scenes and explicit ground truth. Together the line moves from building an evocative closed-loop creature to using artificial ethology as a scored system-identification problem.

nodes.claim: Embeds a small coupled-oscillator/homeostatic controller in a webcam-driven fly so local brightness and texture perturb internal rhythmic state and the resulting control variables continuously shape speed and turning.
nodes.survived: As an historical ancestor, Smartfly supplies the closed-loop embodiment idea that later fly work makes testable: visual evidence changes resident rhythmic state, state changes action, and action changes what is sensed next. The implementation is compact enough to expose its oscillatory variables and intervention knobs directly.
nodes.killed: Later audits do not support taking the apparent behavior stories at face value. FlyBench shows that several intuitive interpretations of the old fly line fail under hidden ground truth and matched controls, while Smarfly2 explicitly abandons the idea that the fly itself should carry the difficult inference. Smartfly's consciousness-style framing therefore remains motivation, not evidence.

nodes.claim: Reverses the old fly-simulation emphasis: keep the fly intentionally small and partially observed, then ask an external temporal observer to recover predictive hidden history from visible world evidence and behavior without access to the fly's hidden state.
nodes.survived: The v0 boundary cleanly separates public observations from hidden audit state and supports matched-present tests. On the sequencing-observer-v1 branch, memory writes are restricted to six visible innovations, four continuation channels advance through active windows separated by dead intervals, slow context modulates susceptibility, route closure is local, and publication is read-only. On the 4,432-frame webcam session, destroying event order or removing context modulation substantially worsens endpoint prediction, so ordered history and contextual susceptibility carry signal even though the complete circuit is not the best predictor.
nodes.killed: The original generic resident observer that low-passed the full visible vector is not supported: it performs badly on the real session. The complete SequencingObserver v1 also does not beat present-only or the 12-frame window on endpoint RMSE, and removing route closure changes little, so the extra circuit has not earned superiority. Tuft/SST/AIS labels remain computational analogies, not biological identification claims.

nodes.claim: Turns the original dumbflies into a reproducible black-box bench with complete hidden ground truth, then asks what outside observers can infer from behavior and controlled scenes before swapping in a real egocentric eye and inherited resonator/window brains.
nodes.survived: The audit shows why a ground-truth bench matters: the original camera contributes almost no predictive information, momentum dominates observable prediction, and where the fly has been explains much more speed than where it is now. The hidden decision-field centroid improves turning prediction further, leaving a concrete recovery gap. After fixing the eye, resonator flies spend more life near the flicker rate matching their inherited tuning, while an untuned window control finds flicker without the same frequency selectivity; the no-breeding test separates tuning from lineage placement.
nodes.killed: Several intuitive stories fail under the answer key: a walking person does not attract the original flies, apparent feeding is not driven by their motion, and darkness does not make them stop. The population-evolution claim is also not established because tuning-frequency enrichment rises in a no-rhythm room as well, consistent with drift in small bottlenecked populations; breeding runs additionally confound spatial sorting through local birth and inherited tuning.

edges.why: Smarfly2 explicitly describes itself as the continuation of the old Dumbflies / SmartFly line after reversing the emphasis: the organism becomes deliberately simple and the external observer becomes the difficult computational object.

Smarfly2's sequencing-observer branch carries the September 27 time-window decomposition into an external observer: selective event deposits feed phase-gated continuation channels, contextual susceptibility changes which continuation is favored, route failure can be locally suppressed, and internal prediction is separated from publication.
